The difference between the richest and poorest regions (281 NUTS-2 regions of the [Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics](/wiki/Nomenclature_of_Territorial_Units_for_Statistics "Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics")) ranged, in 2017, from 31 per cent (Severozapaden, Bulgaria) of the EU28 average (€30,000) to 253 per cent (Luxembourg), or from €4,600 to €92,600.[[181]](#cite_note-200)

The 11 chambers of the Barnenez cairn are of the type known as *[Dolmen](/wiki/Dolmen "Dolmen") à couloir* in French archaeological terminology. The term translates roughly as "[passage grave](/wiki/Passage_grave "Passage grave")". They are built of large slabs of [slate](/wiki/Slate "Slate") and [granite](/wiki/Granite "Granite"). Originally, all the chambers were entirely enclosed by the mound. The fact that several of them are partially exposed now is the result of modern quarrying.

Each of the 11 chambers is reached from the southeast via a long narrow passage (7–12 m long). They are arranged parallel to each other. Shapes and construction techniques differ slightly.

In nine cases, narrow passages lead to [corbelled](/wiki/Corbelling "Corbelling") chambers. Normally, the corbel vault rests on orthostats, in one chamber it actually sits on the ground, forming a true *[tholos](/wiki/Beehive_tomb "Beehive tomb")*. The passages have slab-built or [dry stone walls](/wiki/Dry_stone_wall "Dry stone wall") and are covered with slabs. One of the chambers has a dry-stone vaulted ante-chamber.[[6]](#cite_note-6)
